**What I see:** The ball rises on a much lower arc than before. It peaks at about z ≈ 3.5 m around x ≈ 3 m, then comes down toward the hoop. It reaches rim height a little past the rim centre, at roughly x ≈ 4.2 m. That is level with the back of the rim, just in front of the backboard. From there the copies drop almost straight down to the floor in front of the support, with little forward drift. A clean swish would still be moving forward at about 3 m/s, so the copies would step about 0.3 m (roughly 5 px) per frame. This straight vertical column instead looks like the ball struck the back rim or the backboard and lost its forward speed. In plan view the ball stays on y ≈ 0, so there is no sideways error.

This is close, and at 128 px I cannot rule out that it rattled in off the back rim. My best reading is that it hit the back of the rim or the board and fell outside, which makes it slightly long.

**Fix:** The vertical timing looks right: the ball reaches rim height on the way down. The horizontal reach is about 0.2 m too far, so I reduced vx by about 5% and kept vz.
